subject: Routing proof & subprocessor evidence pack for AtlasHealth - temporary CDN change
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@atlashealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: current subprocessor roster + heads-up on CDN routing change

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this on. AtlasHealth is conducting a quarterly review of all third-party processors that touch EU patient metadata. We need a current roster of subprocessors (names, country, purpose, and whether they handle unredacted logs) and any upcoming changes that could affect EU routing or egress.

We received a brief note from our infra team that CloudLane (one of your CDN partners) may route a small percentage of EU traffic through a US-based fallback for 7–10 days while a regional PoP is upgraded. Can you confirm whether Redwood plans that change, approximate dates, and provide any evidence of onshore handling controls (KMS jurisdiction, access logs, export controls)?

For our SOC/contract team, please include a single bundle (zip) with the current roster and any evidence you can share.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our deadline is next Monday, 9/17 EOD CET.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Security Operations
AtlasHealth

Stephanie / team — quick note on KMS and jurisdiction: CloudLane’s fallback path uses ephemeral wrapping keys that are generated in our us-west KMS region for the duration of the failover. Data-at-rest for the cached edge objects remains encrypted; however, the transit buffers for log collection are routed via CloudLane’s US ingestion endpoints for up to 72 hours during the swap.

I’m attaching a short memo that summarizes controls and a suggested redline to our standard DPA language that clarifies temporary routing and key jurisdiction for customers with EU residency requirements. If Atlas needs a more formal onshore attestation (signed), we can provide that via our security team.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Stephanie / Kimberly — thanks for the quick reply and the memo. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

1) For the temporary routing window, can you provide a concrete date range for the failover and a simple routing flow diagram that shows where customer-origin IPs and logs transit (we only need the path and whether logs hit a US endpoint).
2) We will need proof that keys used during the failover are ephemeral and that persistent encryption keys remain under EU jurisdiction for AtlasHealth customer data. A stamped PDF or statement is fine.
3) Regarding logs: please include a sample redacted transit log (timestamped) and a checklist of which logs may include IPs or other identifiers during the failover.

If you can get this to us by 9/17 EOD CET that will keep the review on schedule.

Best,
Elena
